title: First Amendment Retaliation — Dr. Elena Vasquez v. State University Board of Regents
facts: Dr. Elena Vasquez, a tenured professor of Political Science at State University, published an op-ed in the Washington Post on March 3, 2025, criticizing the university's decision to accept a $50 million donation from a foreign government with a documented record of human rights abuses. The op-ed argued the donation created conflicts of interest in the university's Middle Eastern Studies department. On March 20, 2025, the Board of Regents voted to revoke Dr. Vasquez's tenure and terminate her employment, citing 'conduct unbecoming of a faculty member' and 'violation of institutional loyalty obligations.' Dr. Vasquez alleges her termination violates the First Amendment's protection of free speech, as State University is a public institution and her op-ed addressed a matter of public concern. She cites Pickering v. Board of Education (1968) and Garcetti v. Ceballos (2006), arguing her speech was made as a private citizen on a public matter, not as part of her official duties. The university argues the op-ed contained confidential donor information obtained through her committee role, that the speech was made pursuant to her official duties and thus not protected under Garcetti, and that the termination followed standard disciplinary procedures. The case involves a direct tension between faculty free speech rights at public universities, the scope of Garcetti's 'official duties' exception, and institutional autonomy — a constitutional question that has produced conflicting precedents across federal circuits. The Third Circuit and Ninth Circuit have reached opposite conclusions on whether Garcetti applies to academic speech at public universities.
supporting_materials: Tenure contract and faculty handbook provisions on academic freedom. The published op-ed dated March 3, 2025. Board of Regents meeting minutes from March 20, 2025. Prior performance reviews (all exemplary). Documentation showing the op-ed was written outside university time and facilities. Evidence that the donor information was publicly available through IRS 990 filings. Amicus briefs from the ACLU and the American Association of University Professors. Conflicting circuit court opinions: Demers v. Austin (9th Cir. 2014) vs. Gorum v. Sessoms (3rd Cir. 2009) on Garcetti's application to academic speech.
